newsitem.title: UK: Three more tankers to load Iraqi crude from Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Three more tankers to load Iraqi crude from Turkey.

text.p: At least three more crude oil tankers are expected to load Iraqi crude from the Turkish port of Ceyhan before the end of this month, shipping sources said on Thursday.
Ship brokers and other sources said that the the 142,000 deadweight tonne (dwt) Tito Tapias had been chartered by Elf to load Iraqi crude on December 21, and it was expected to sail to Lavera.

They also thought that the 142,000 dwt Marble had been chartered by Spain's Repsol to load on December 24, and added that they expected either the Oak or the Saturn to load 130,000 tonnes on December 30 with options to sail to northwest Europe or other Mediterranean destinations.
One broker said he thought Shell had made the latter fixture.

These three vessels will follow the Gole, which was the first ship to load Iraqi crude since the approval of the $2 billion U.N. oil-for-food deal. It sailed from Ceyhan on Monday with 153,500 tonnes of Kirkuk crude, destined for Turkey's western refinery at Aliaga.
Iraqi crude is pumped via pipeline to Ceyhan, and is also being exported from the terminal of Mina al-Bakr in southern Iraq.

The 272,000 dwt Leonidas sailed from al-Bakr on Thursday and it is headed for a north American destination, shipping sources said. The 274,000 dwt Star Africa sailed on Tuesday, and it is headed for the Caribbean, they added.
Brokers said on Wednesday they thought Petrodiamond was due to load 250,000 tonnes of Iraqi crude from al-Bakr on January 24. The vessel was expected to sail to Japan.
It was not immediately clear which vessels were likely to load at al-Bakr between now and then.
